classification: PAPER STORY FREEZE. Experimental protocol. Not PAPER-FAITHFUL. Does not authorize a new architecture, a learned router, or online opponent inference. Does not reopen DUAL_BRANCH_ROLE_COMPOSITE_V1.
decided_by: PI, 2026-10-01/02: freeze one end-to-end paper story and stop adding architectural branches. Same research program, stronger architecture: repair the A-only role asymmetry; keep specialists, poles, crossover, deltas, scaling, CLOSEST_DEFENDS, and the sharing ladder.
CHARACTERIZATION: Same research program, stronger architecture. Not a new project. Skeleton stays specialists -> team organization -> crossover -> parameter sharing / z. The middle layer changes from A-only roles to identical ATTACK/DEFEND machinery on A and B.
CENTRAL_CLAIM: strategy != role. Roles answer who does what. z answers what overall team behavior is being executed.
PIPELINE_boxed: opponent demand -> role-organized strategic teachers -> shared latent strategic representation
THE_QUESTION: Can explicit role organization preserve distinct opponent-conditioned strategies as multi-agent teams scale, and can those strategies subsequently be represented within a shared policy through a compact latent strategic representation?

DISTINCTION_locked.roles: organize agents (what job does this agent have?)
DISTINCTION_locked.z: which team strategy is being expressed (discrete strategic mode), not an inferred opponent identity
DISTINCTION_locked.not_the_same_thing: roles are the scaffold that keeps a strategy coherent as N grows; they are not the strategy

1_different_strategic_demands.artifacts: repaired 1M specialists pi_A and pi_B at N in {2,4,6} (FOUNDATION_CHECKPOINTS in DUAL_BRANCH_ROLE_COMPOSITE_V1_SPEC.json)
1_different_strategic_demands.question: Do Pole A (OP6) and Pole B (OP7) create different strategic demands?

2_make_strategies_scalable.construction: for each s in {A,B}: pi_s -> {pi_s,ATTACK, pi_s,DEFEND}, both warm-started from the same specialist, one joint 200k env-step PPO run, k=ceil(N/3), CLOSEST_DEFENDS, roles fixed for the episode
2_make_strategies_scalable.question: Does explicit team organization allow those strategic responses to remain coherent at 2v2, 4v4, and 6v6?

3_prove_they_are_different_strategies.primary: reproducible behavioral differentiation interpretable vs OP6 vs OP7, plus a functional measure (crossover) showing the distinction matters
3_prove_they_are_different_strategies.not_required: Delta_A, Delta_B >> 0 as the sole success definition
3_prove_they_are_different_strategies.eval_order: fresh DEV n=64 then confirmatory n=128; neither block overlaps exploratory top-50

4_one_shared_strategic_representation.starts_only_after: Stage 2 teachers seal and Stage 3 freezes them as the distillation teachers

symbols.z: strategy-conditioned latent mode in {z_A, z_B}, supplied externally, learned as embeddings inside the shared network

distillation_example.not: observation + strategy only, with role identity dropped

4_one_shared_strategic_representation.deployment: select z_A or z_B and assign r by CLOSEST_DEFENDS(ceil(N/3)); do not infer z from opponent history
4_one_shared_strategic_representation.what_this_tests: Can one shared policy encode and preserve distinct strategic modes, and is z necessary once the agent already knows its role?
4_one_shared_strategic_representation.naming: latent strategic representation or strategy-conditioned latent mode. Do not say the network autonomously discovered two latent strategies.
sharing_ladder_remove_information: Separated: four teacher branches A_ATTACK, A_DEFEND, B_ATTACK, B_DEFEND
Fully shared + strategy z + role r: pi(a | o, z, r)
Role only: pi(a | o, r), strategy z removed
4_one_shared_strategic_representation.role_only_question: If the model still knows it is ATTACK or DEFEND but no longer knows Strategy A vs Strategy B, is role information enough, or is a distinct strategic representation necessary?
4_one_shared_strategic_representation.fully_shared_question: Can one network preserve both strategies when told which strategic mode to execute and which role this agent has?
4_one_shared_strategic_representation.teachers_must_be: the sealed dual-branch role composites from Stage 2, not historical frozen-ATTACK pi_DA / pi_DB

chain: roles preserve/organize them as N increases
shared z can represent both without collapsing them
SUCCESS_for_the_paper.performance: evidence that the strategies are meaningful; behavioral differentiation is central
allowed_readings: similar win rates with distinct, repeatable signatures (broader pressure vs concentrated/reactive) that survive into Fully Shared+z
role-only (no z) keeps a good win rate but loses A vs B signatures: role organization is not the same as preserving two strategies
a scale where organization fails (e.g. 6v6) reported as a scaling result under the frozen construction

EXPLICITLY_NOT_IN_THIS_PAPER: q_phi(z | opponent history) or any learned router
per-scale architecture changes after seeing results
reopening dual-branch ATTACK/DEFEND losses, k, or the 200k joint budget
treating historical sharing-ladder runs (defender-only teachers, k=N/2 at 4v4) as this paper's Stage 4

HISTORICAL_SHARING_SPECS.status: exploratory provenance under earlier teachers; not Stage 4 of this story
HISTORICAL_SHARING_SPECS.why_not_reused: those arms distilled defender-only / asymmetric composites and, at 4v4, held k=N/2. This paper's teachers are dual-branch with k=ceil(N/3) on both A and B.

ORDER_do_not_reorder: symmetric dual-branch role training, 200k joint env steps per strategy, all N
Separated teachers; then Share-Encoder; Fully shared + z + r; role r only (no z)
evaluate behavioral strategy preservation plus crossover / win-rate / score evidence
